source.title: Understanding and Improving Early Stopping for Learning with Noisy Labels
source.authors: Ying-Long Bai; Er-Kun Yang; Bo Han; Yanhua Yang; Jiatong Li; Yi-Nian Mao; Gang Niu; Tong-Liang Liu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses the memorization effect to motivate progressive early stopping and reports its method's performance. It does not test the listed random-label fitting claims.
record.gate_note: The paper measures how noisy-label training affects representations at different layers over training epochs. Those results concern a related layer-sensitivity finding, not the behaviors named in V1–V6. Reported classification tables compare PES and other methods on noisy-label datasets; they do not measure the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses the real-labels-first memorization effect to develop progressive early stopping. Its own experiments measure layerwise representation quality and mitigation performance, without measuring clean-label versus noisy-label fitting over training. These results do not test V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that noisy labels affect later layers earlier and more severely, motivating progressive early stopping. They report improved noisy-label classification performance and identify additional hyperparameters requiring careful tuning as the method's main limitation.
record.recipe_differences: Progressive early stopping separates networks into parts and trains them for different epoch counts; this study addresses learning with noisy labels rather than fitting fully random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured layerwise trajectories vary by layer and network depth; the paper also reports sensitivity to T2 and T3.

fits_no_version.finding: Representations in later layers generally reach their best evaluated performance earlier and deteriorate more with continued noisy-label training; earlier-layer representations remain more stable. Layer timing differences are less apparent in LeNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noisy-label training affects later-layer representation quality earlier and more severely than earlier-layer representation quality, with timing differences depending on network depth and task.

record.problems: The layerwise findings are presented in figures without numerical values in the supplied text; reported curves are means of five runs. The study does not evaluate fully random labels or training error.
record.rows_left_out: None of the qualifying layerwise figure conditions were left out.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error on fully random labels, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Time to fit random versus true labels and convergence speed across corruption fractions. Table 6 compares mitigation methods at one noise level instead.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit together with steadily worsening test error across corruption fractions from zero to complete randomization. Benchmark test accuracies alone do not establish this conjunction.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting and whether removing it harms true-label generalization.
The temporal ordering of fitting shared clean patterns and memorizing noisy labels. The study assumes this ordering but does not separately measure their fitting trajectories.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains figure captions and qualitative descriptions, but no readable plotted values. Qualitative layerwise trends are established; cannot_determine refers to the listed claim versions. Figure 5's merged vertical markers indicate coincident best epochs, not coincident accuracy trajectories.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label training error, chance test error, and whether fitting requires changes to the architecture or hyperparameters.
Training time to fit random versus true labels and convergence as the fraction of corrupted labels grows.
Fitting shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and test error across corruption fractions from none to all.
Whether regularization or data augmentation prevents random-label fitting, or whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Whether networks learn patterns in real labels before memorizing noisy or random labels.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Measure classification performance from representations at the 9-th layer after training on noisy labels for different epochs; evaluate by fixing that layer and preceding layers, then reinitializing and optimizing the rest with clean data.
rows.measure: Classification performance across training epochs; precise values are figure only.
rows.uncertainty: Mean of five runs; no error bar stated.
rows.note: The paper describes former-layer representations as relatively robust; precise plotted values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Clean-data retraining evaluates representation quality, not any version's fitting behavior.
